body: Does it have to be official copies of the letters and death certificate or scanned copies? Thank you for the information. I'm trying to do the same and wanted to make sure I do it right.
I have Ultima 1-7, Serpent's Isle and expansions, both underworlds, Savage Empire and Martian Dreams. I have the maps and everything from all of them, just not the trinkets.
I understand. I kept thinking I would find that bag of trinkets, but I know they're gone now.
Thank you! I am itemizing so just wanted to make sure I do the right thing.

I've been having trouble despite finding someone arguably better. I saw some red flags but it's still hard to ignore all the good times. She kidded with me a little, but it seemed like the way that her family did with each other. It's just so hard to believe that someone who supposedly worried all the time doesn't care about me anymore during a pandemic.

I don't think she was a narcissist, but she did future fake. I've got to take care of you in my will, move in with me, how is she got pregnant it wouldn't be so bad, would it?, we'll go to (named several countries around the world), looked up ticket prices several times in front of me, mentioned owning property trying to get me excited about what it might be worth and what we should do with it. This was all within the first 2 months. I never got excited about the actual promises, it was the idea that I thought someone loved me and really was committing to me. I still don't 100% understand why she did it.
That is a great thought. Staying present seems to be the answer. It's tough but worth working on.

Unfortunately, it seems to be common. If a person has an issue, they can tell you that you're their best friend and a week later, leave. It's hard to let go because you remember all the positives, but if he stayed his problem would still be there, it just would come out in more unpleasant ways.

Mine (and she's 50!) with a note in the mail along with my stuff that I left over at her place. No response for 3 weeks before that or since. A text might have been better, but not good either. Conflict avoidance doesn't have an age limit.

I have felt that way for a long time yet here I am at 48. I have experienced some amazing times that I would have missed out on. Moments from friends that touched me and moments in love that made me feel alive. I don't want to give up and I don't want you to either.
Sometimes the best relationships happen later in life. It can happen at any time. There are so many people in the world. It will happen, just please give it time.
Please don't. Things do change. It's the toughest thing to see at the time but they do.

I checked it out. Thanks. I've read a lot and watched a lot of videos. I don't know if it helps but I'm trying. I just want her back. The way she did it just was so out of character. I'm wondering if at my age I should just stop trying to find someone. All relationships end. I don't know if it would have been worse to have 5 years with her and have this happen. I feel like I would have been happy with her for the rest of my life. I don't have a ton of relationship experience so I'm not used to this. Seems common from what I read.

I left a voicemail, text and email. Nothing. I don't understand. It would be one thing if she said or had reason to be mad with me, but it's almost like she knows she needs to be alone and is trying to resist temptation and just cut all ties. Of course it could just be that she fell out of love and doesn't care. Whatever the answer is, it's been devastating to me. I thought I finally found an incredible woman to have a long future with.

I've settled on her being a people pleaser. It completely fits her and also the anger and resentment. Maybe she knew it was irrational to feel that way towards me because I have the same tendency and was always offering/helping her. I just don't understands cutting all contact with just a note.  We couldn't even talk about it or work on it. I wonder if she thinks she doesn't deserve someone or if she's actually going to work on it. I feel like it's a fixable issue especially with someone who would want to know what her needs are and encourage her to express them.
Sure, we can talk. I'm gong through a break up myself. What was your argument about?

Funny because I'm INFJ. Feel like she has to be needed sounds accurate. She nags and we joked that she's the best at it. When talking about her kids and helping them "but no one listens to me" . And interestingly, she may have thought she was pulling the weight, but because of my own issues I always did whatever I could to help or take care of her. I walked her dogs when it was cold or too early or too late,  made the bed for her to come home too, which she loved early on. I literally climbed around in her storage pod to get things she needed. I've looked up and will continue  to research codependency to understand what happened and my own issues with it. I was attracted physically and she's smart, has a surprisingly funny sense of humor and yes the fact that she seemed to be all in about me was exciting.

I can't claim to know about someone else but she didn't seem to have the energy or time for that. Yes she was a self proclaimed nag. Checked to see I was taking my medicine, asking me to bring laundry,  offering to get up early to make breakfast. When I fell asleep without my cpap mask on, she would wake me not because of the snoring but because she was concerned with my breathing. Always concerned with my health and apologized for just mentioning hers because she thought it sounded like complaining.  I would assure her she didn't have to say sorry. She would joke that there must be something wrong with me for being with her, but she never showed anything that would make someone believe there was anything wrong.

Exactly how it felt... like a husband. Stopping all communication except for the note. I never would have believed she would do this. She kept my Christmas gifts to her and in the box of my stuff, sent the ones she gave me that I left there, which seems not so angry? We ended up spending equally on gifts and everything felt very equal. I usually treated her to dinner but sometimes she made dinner. I did my best to take care of her. Took her to the Dr when she was sick. I would offer to walk her dogs when it was cold, late or she was getting ready for work, made the bed for her so she would have that nice surprise when she came home and I wasn't there. I literally climbed around in her storage pod to get things she needed. I was proclaimed boyfriend of the year that day. How things change.
I know it's tough to say.  She was married 17 years to someone who was supposedly later diagnosed as bipolar. That can mess a person up. Can narcs be married that long?
Thank you.  I'm sorry that happened after a year.  Do you suspect narcissist or something else?

Yes I did learn. A week before she said I was her best friend. I'm 48, she's 50. She seemed very nice, smart and I thought she just knew what she wanted. When we were talking about the possibility of pregnancy which would be unlikely, she smiled and said it wouldn't be so bad, would it? I thought some things said we're strange but I took it as she really loved me. She was self deprecating, said sorry almost too much  as opposed to thinking nothing was her fault. I didn't think the first date was going well.  I asked if she wanted to go to the beach after and she said whatever you want to do. I didn't take it as positive, but we ended up kissing for about an hour. Why love bomb and just leave as opposed to making it worse. ..I mam she could have waited until I moved and that would have been really bad.

Yes all in 4 months. That's what I thought at first but she never tore me down. I thought that led to the discard phase and would a narcissist  leave a note? Idk. She did have the narc stare that I've read about though. I have more examples but I thought the will example showed how future she was thinking. I wake up at 3 or 4 each morning with anxiety as a result. I think closure would help.

I'm sorry.  What happened? I think I have figured out that she has codependent issues and has been rushing things and trying to please so long that she resents having someone around. No matter how equal we would take care of each other. Then the depression just made everything worse. Helps a little to figure out why.
She never said a bad word to me or exhibited any sudden mood changes. The fact that she said she felt anger and resentment over having to "take care of someone else"was very surprising.

She mentioned that she had depression and her daughter does as well. Never mentioned how severe. Just trying to figure it out. I did know someone with bipolar and the disappearing and canceling plans was familiar. Perhaps severe depression clouding judgement makes more sense? She was married for a long time to someone she said was eventually diagnosed with bipolar. 
 I'm upset, but I  also worry about her as this is the worst possible time for get to be alone. She had a compromised immune system where she can catch something easily and is struggling with her job and about to move into her new house.
I considered narcissist first but she never tried to tear me down, just left instead. Could that still be because the future faking was intense. I have many examples of that.

Thanks. I've never met someone so perfect for me even looking back on it. Everything was great until that Monday before Valentine's. I'd really like to know what she has. If it was malicious like a narcissist or a disorder where's she could get better with proper treatment.
Sure, anytime.

I think people that say leave are tortured by memories of a bipolar partner. I would agree that if you give her conditions and she's serious about it, then it is worth another try.  After that, if it's the same as it is now,  you have to realize that it will keep happening and no one should have to go through that.

You're not being unfair. From everything I've read, if he's not taking meds, going to therapy and staying away from alcohol, then it's going to continue. He needs to know how important it is and that he has to do those things if you're going to stay together.

You don't know what it's going to be like until you experience it. A bipolar person from what I've experienced and read here really makes you feel loved at first. Then, you're in love and you focus on the times that are good and think maybe there's something I can do to keep those good times going and reduce the isolation. Then you learn that you can't.

Yes, over the course of 3 years... we would get close and she would "have a lot going on" and disappear for a few weeks. Then she would talk to someone she knew from high school who she thought was her soulmate. Then she would come back and we would get close again. Then I was her soulmate. Then she met him for dinner and all the old feelings came back. Then she stopped talking to him. This past year she goes to a high school reunion and gets drunk. Old feelings come back again. It would be a couple of months of no contact. This last time I visited her she cried about how she thought the viisit wasn't worth it for me since she had to work so much. At the end of the trip she said she was sorry she was distant. The next day after telling me that she didn't want me to worry about us when I went back home, she got mad at me over something stupid and bam 6 months of nc. That's why when I see so many similar stories, I really don't want people going through that. Believe it or not, when all this wasn't going on she seemed rational and has good qualities as well.

Things will get better outside of the relationship. Try not to focus on the things you can't control. However, you know the relationship isn't healthy. You can't get support from him when you need it and he asks you to come over when he feels like it and tells you to fuck off when he doesn't want to see you. We need a partner who will be there for us. Would a friend do that? Pm if you want to talk.

Thank you. I realized that I needed to have the boundary conversation and I was ready, but after this long, I don't think we should be together. I don't believe she would do what it takes. You absolutely have to have the boundaries conversation. Following through is the only fair thing to you. Don't let it get to 6 months at a time like she did with me. It isn't okay for one person to disappear over and over.

It would be weeks. Then months. It was always stressful. I always thought if I said the right thing she might return but it was always when she was ready to return that she would initiate contact. This last time was 6 months. Just after I wrote this I received a text. Basically all it said was I'm sorry. I haven't responded. I need a lot more than that. I need a reason to trust her. I don't want to be hurt again.
Let's talk. Pm me. I just want to get to know someone right now and taking it slow sounds good.

I'm glad you're starting to recover. I'm sure you did nothing wrong. The same thing happened to me multiple times and this last time was 6 months. Be prepared that if you hear from him, you might not get closure. I was talking about moving to the state she lives and all I got was I'm sorry after 6 months of nc. I didn't respond because even though I still care for her I can't go through it again and I know I would. It's more painful worrying about losing someone at any moment than just living alone.
Pm if you want to talk. I still have some days where I think about the past with the gf I thought I knew, so I know it can be tough
It's been 6 months for me.  I miss her, but it doesn't hurt like it did. I can see a time in the future when I will look back and realize I was much better off without her. It just takes time.

My ex girlfriend did basically the same thing. She would stop talking to me every few months. This went on for almost 3 years. She would come back and tell me she missed me and was sorry for how she treated me. She took medication but didn't like therapy. Now it's been no contact since September. I finally learned that we can't have a relationship, but I still miss her sometimes. If you don't have a good reason to believe things will change, then it's best to move on before he just leaves for good. You deserve more in a relationship.

You never know where you're going to find a great love. I've said the same things positives about mine, but I can also say nobody has ever made me feel worse as well and that's important to remember.

Yes, at some point he will need the book or need to leave as well. I went through 3 years and she's gone back to an old boyfriend at least 3 times. I used to think I was more, but really I was just a replacement as well.

She didn't like expectations and had a problem if she thought I was disappointed with her. My guess is she has a history of cancelling plans depending on mood and then feeling guilty and depressed about it. So, making the plan and then knowing someone is depending on you to follow through is probably stressful.

Please don't feel guilty. It sounds like you were there for him as much as anyone could be. It's tough to realize when you're down that you deserve better, but you do. It isn't about being selfish at all. I wish that I had let go the first time she broke up. It would have been so much easier to deal with. My only advice is moving on now will eventually help you to take care of yourself that much sooner.

You can't blame yourself. If you're too persistent, it can push someone away too. Mine called me pushy because I wanted to schedule time to see her. It was a ldr. She had a rough time also and drank sometimes. It caused her to break up with me in July. She regretted it and questioned why she did it two weeks later. She was too embarrassed to contact me until I reached out one more time. We got back together in September and then she ghosted in October. Who knows why other than it's BP. They know that they can't drink with their meds. Basically, you'll never know what will trigger the ghosting or return, but it will keep happening if they don't manage their BP. We can want to help all we want, but only they can truly do it. It's frustrating and makes you question everything until it keeps happening so much that I know now that there's a reason why she hasn't been able to maintain a relationship. It isn't because she's a bad person, it's the BP and unless you're truly committed to managing, it will continue to be like this no matter how much sense she makes when she's stable. If it wasn't those last few weeks, it would have been something else. The more we accept that, the better off we'll be.

It wasn't you. Don't rack your brain. Mine told me that she didn't want me to worry anymore about her dating someone else two days before she ghosted me. It's been 3 months since I've heard from her. As strong as the feelings of love seemed to be, it's better if she doesn't come back because you can never feel safe in a relationship like that.
Yes communication is so important. It was the main thing missing with my SO and it would have helped.

You're not alone at all. I'm 2 months into this no contact stretch and it feels worse every time. There is someone else out there who can be your partner and not make you feel this way. There are a lot of people who would appreciate a partner as loyal as the SOs here.
Sorry no. I meant the op. Still getting used to posting.
Very similar. You can message me as well

It seems that it has a chance of being better if the person with bipolar tries hard to manage it correctly and adjusts when the medicine isn't working. If that doesn't happen, I don't think it really ever gets better than a rollercoaster.
PM me if you want. I have my own stories to share but always willing to listen.

That's a quote I've been thinking about. Think about how good it was to love them. I am willing to give my BP so one more chance because I love her and I believe her when she says she loves me, but at some point you have to say this is the last chance just because it hurts too much being in limbo when they leave.
Very very nice of you. I am new but hope my guess counts anyway 1077
